title: Meet: for item in list
idea: Introduce the exact syntax 'for item in list:' with visible, predictable output — each value printed in turn.

exercises.prompt:
Here is the new tool:

scores = [10, 7, 9]
for score in scores:
    print(score)

What does 'score' hold on each pass of the loop?
options: One value from the list, in order: first 10, then 7, then 9
exercises.explanation: 'for score in scores' hands you each value in turn. First pass score is 10, next 7, next 9.

exercises.prompt:
scores = [10, 7, 9]
for score in scores:
    print(score)

What is printed?
options: 10, then 7, then 9 — each on its own line
exercises.explanation: The print runs once per value, so you see 10, 7, 9 on three lines. No totalling — each value is simply shown.

exercises.prompt: In 'for score in scores:', the name 'score' is a variable YOU choose — it just holds the current value each time around.
exercises.explanation: You pick the loop-variable name. 'score' reads nicely because the list is called scores and holds scores.

exercises.prompt:
Fill the blank so the loop visits every price in the list:

prices = [3, 5, 2]
for price ____ prices:
    print(price)
exercises.explanation: The shape is 'for <name> in <list>:'. The keyword 'in' connects your loop variable to the list.

exercises.prompt: Why does the body line 'print(score)' need to be indented (pushed right)?
options: Indentation shows it belongs INSIDE the loop, so it runs each pass
It makes the code prettier only
It makes the loop run once
exercises.explanation: Just like with if and range-loops, indentation marks the body — the lines done on every pass.

exercises.prompt: Arrange these lines so each value in the list is printed.
exercises.explanation: First make the list, then start the loop header, then the indented body. Prints 1, 2, 3.

exercises.prompt:
temps = [18, 21]
for t in temps:
    print(t)
    print("done")

How many lines are printed in total?
options: Four — the body has two prints and runs twice
exercises.explanation: Two items, and the body prints twice per pass, so 2 x 2 = 4 lines: 18, done, 21, done.

exercises.prompt: If the list is empty, like items = [], the loop body runs zero times.
exercises.explanation: No items means nothing to visit, so the body never runs. An empty list is a perfectly valid list.

exercises.prompt:
nums = [4, 8, 1]
for n in nums:
    print(n)

Which value does the loop variable hold on the LAST pass?
exercises.explanation: The loop walks front to back, so the last pass holds the last value, 1.

exercises.prompt: Build the loop header that visits every value in a list called ages. (Tap the tokens in order.)
exercises.explanation: for age in ages: — pick a readable loop-variable name (age), use 'in', name the list, end with a colon.
